craft_notes: Sthāyin: praṇaya proof against aversion (intimacy surviving hate). Sanskrit hammers three 1pl verbs, then tenders dearness, then the held-all. Device: dash-hold on the hammer, colon landing on the held-all (wonder lands). Bright: counsel taken, lightly won, shouldered all — kept glowing, hate kept unsmoothed. Rejected: softening loathe→dislike — killed: Vṛtti reads dveṣa itself as tvanmaya (His-stuff), softening betrays the daring; 'dear Lord' address — killed: tenderness earned only after the hammer, importing it early decorates; breaking into short lines — killed: staccato mimics rage, but this is confession past rage. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: You we loathe, you we laud, with you we take counsel — O Ambikā's lord,
how lightly won, how well: the all you shouldered for us.
l4.sanskrit_cite: dviṣmas tvāṃ tvāṃ stumas tubhyaṃ mantrayāmo 'mbikāpate ativāllabhyataḥ sādhu viśvaṅ no dhṛtavān asi

reads_against.argmap: We hate you, we praise you; to you we address (tubhyam mantrayāmaḥ).; By great accessibility, well done: the all you have held for us (Kṣemarāja M00089: praise is realization of the non-dual Lord appearing in diversity). → Hate and praise are both address to Ambikā's husband, who holds the all.
c1_essence: Milk-ocean Śaṅkara bowed; hate and praise both address Ambikā's husband who holds the all.
reads_against.c1_rasa: bhakti-vismaya (devotion charged with wonder); sthayibhava utsāha-in-bhakti
